name: Greta Thunberg
summary: Greta Thunberg calls for immediate cuts in greenhouse-gas emissions and an end to fossil fuel expansion. She argues that wealthy countries must act faster and has opposed wind development that violates Sámi rights. She has also called for an end to the Israeli occupation of Palestinian territories and joined civilian flotillas seeking to deliver aid to Gaza.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Thunberg and her co-authors condemned Hamas’s killings of Israeli civilians and rejected those killings as a justification for violence against Palestinian civilians.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: In “The science is as solid as it gets,” Thunberg describes affluent overconsumption as a habit normalised over generations that contributes to ecological damage.

corporate-influence.rationale: In “We are not moving in the right direction,” Thunberg argues that fossil fuel companies benefit from climate delay and that lobbyists for short-term economic interests have too much control over policy.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: In “What needs to be done,” Thunberg describes the climate crisis as a form of historic racial injustice and calls on the countries that drove it to pay for the resulting harm.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: In her COP25 address collected in No One Is Too Small to Make a Difference and in “What can you do as an individual,” she describes democracy as continuous public participation and calls for defending expression and expanding participation between elections.

direct-action.rationale: In her European Parliament address, she described school strikes as a way for children to draw attention to climate change and explicitly called on eligible citizens to use their votes to protect future generations.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In her 2019 UN address she demands immediate emissions cuts. Her joint article with Christiana Figueres calls on governments to accelerate cuts and replace coal power and internal combustion engines.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: At COP24 she demanded that fossil fuels stay in the ground. At Davos she called for an immediate halt to investment in exploration and extraction.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In the family discussion of population and nuclear power in Our House Is on Fire, Thunberg argues for investing in wind and solar over building new reactors, citing costs, lead times and waste storage. Her 2022 comments addressed retaining plants already in service.

future-generations.rationale: At the 2019 UN Climate Action Summit she holds leaders accountable to future generations for the effects of their emissions choices. In I Know This to Be True she explains that her strike demands action consistent with the Paris Agreement to protect children’s future.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: Thunberg attributes present warming to human activity in her Amanpour interview. In “The science is as solid as it gets” she traces the climate crisis to the activities and economic structures that drive human emissions.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Thunberg took part in blockading a Norwegian ministry during the Fosen dispute and identified returning the reindeer-herding land to the Sámi as a central demand of the action.

limit-growth.rationale: At COP24 she rejected perpetual green growth as a response to the crisis. In The Climate Book she calls for changing affluent ways of life to reduce emissions and argues that economic growth has failed to deliver those cuts.

limit-population.rationale: In “The science is as solid as it gets,” she calls the argument that there are too many people misleading and puts responsibility on the consumption and economic structures of the high-emitting minority.

nation-first.rationale: In her European Parliament address she urges leaders to set aside national differences and cooperate in the climate emergency. In “What needs to be done” she argues that high-emitting countries owe compensation for damage caused abroad.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: In “The science is as solid as it gets,” she argues that humans have no greater claim to the Earth than other species and treats the crisis as affecting all living beings.

participatory-democracy.rationale: In “What can you do as an individual” she calls for broadening democratic participation through institutions such as citizens’ assemblies, alongside elections.

precautionary-principle.rationale: She urged the European Parliament to act immediately on the risk of irreversible climate feedbacks, explicitly acknowledging that no one knew exactly when the tipping points would occur.

state-directs-investment.rationale: In “We are not moving in the right direction,” she urges governments to direct recovery spending toward clean energy and other effective climate investments and condemns subsidising coal, oil and gas.

notes: Reviewed all current statements against the available record. Searched economy (growth, consumption, investment, taxation and labour), government (elections, assemblies, court challenges and lobbying), society and culture (Indigenous land, racial justice and equal rights), world and globalism (Gaza, Ukraine, occupation, international law and climate finance), liberty and means (protest, disobedience, penalties and nonviolence), ecology (warming, fuel extraction, population and biodiversity), and technology (new reactors, carbon capture and technical fixes). Used the six locally catalogued texts, searched the Davos, European speech and CNN/NPR corpora, and checked recent interviews and coverage. The family memoir records her objections to constructing new reactors. Her later Germany remarks concern retaining existing plants during a coal substitution. The Climate Book evidence is from her signed chapters. Her climate compensation proposals address damage from historical emissions. Her Gaza sources condemn civilian killings, but do not specify refugee-return law or whether any people are entitled to a state. The case-specific record on court fines does not settle what protesters ought to do about penalties in general. This Codex pass was directly requested while the preceding same-day pass was being integrated.
